review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

5:1.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρέτ,
5:1.targetText: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God,

groups.note: The narrative formula Ἐγένετο δέ ("now it came about") is rendered On one occasion.
ἐν τῷ with the infinitive ("while the crowd was pressing") is rendered as the with-phrase.
The καί that brings in the main clause after ἐγένετο is rendered while; BSB makes Jesus' standing the while-clause.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτός ("he").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the second infinitive as purpose (to hear) and leaves this καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:2.sourceText: καὶ εἶδεν πλοῖα δύο ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην· οἱ δὲ ἁλεεῖς ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα.
5:2.targetText: He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.

groups.note: παρά ("beside") is rendered at the edge of.
Same noun, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text (N1904: ἁλεεῖς).
ἀποβάντες ἀπ’ ("having stepped away from") is rendered had left.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render ἑστῶτα ("standing"); at the edge of gives the boats' position.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause (had left them) to the main verb ἔπλυνον.

5:3.sourceText: ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων, ὃ ἦν Σίμωνος, ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον· καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν τοὺς ὄχλους.
5:3.targetText: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore. And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.

groups.note: ἓν τῶν πλοίων ("one of the boats") is rendered the boat, identified by its owner.
The relative clause ὃ ἦν ("which was") with the genitive Σίμωνος is rendered belonging to Simon.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle ἐμβάς.
English joins the participle clause (got into the boat) to the main verb ἠρώτησεν.

5:4.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν, εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα Ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος, καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν.
5:4.targetText: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἐπαύσατο.

5:5.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν Ἐπιστάτα, δι’ ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν· ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω τὰ δίκτυα.
5:5.targetText: “Master,” Simon replied, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered by one verb.
δι’ ὅλης νυκτός ("through the whole night") is rendered all night.
BSB makes the participle κοπιάσαντες the main verb.
οὐδέν ("nothing") is rendered without … anything.
The finite ἐλάβομεν ("we took") is rendered as the without-phrase catching.
ἐπὶ τῷ ῥήματί σου ("at your word") is rendered because You say so.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:6.sourceText: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ· διερήσσετο δὲ τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν.
5:6.targetText: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.

groups.note: The participle ποιήσαντες ("having done") is rendered as a When-clause.
πολύ ("great") is rendered such … large, setting up the result clause.
Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text; the imperfect ("was tearing") is rendered began to tear.
BSB turns the δέ clause into a result clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:7.sourceText: καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἦλθαν, καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά.
5:7.targetText: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.

groups.note: The dative μετόχοις supplies to.
The article τοῦ with the infinitive συλλαβέσθαι expresses purpose.
The participle ἐλθόντας ("coming") is rendered as an infinitive.
Same verb; BSB's Greek text has a different form of it here (N1904: ἦλθαν).
The present infinitive βυθίζεσθαι ("to be sinking") is rendered began to sink.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐλθόντας to the infinitive συλλαβέσθαι.
English adds full to the result clause; ἔπλησαν (filled) already says it.

5:8.sourceText: ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων Ἔξελθε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, Κύριε.
5:8.targetText: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees. “Go away from me, Lord,” he said, “for I am a sinful man.”

groups.note: The participle ἰδών ("having seen") is rendered as a When-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for saw; ἰδών has none.

5:9.sourceText: θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ᾗ συνέλαβον,
5:9.targetText: For he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken,

groups.note: θάμβος περιέσχεν ("amazement seized") is rendered were astonished.
τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ("those with him") is rendered his companions.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render πάντας ("all").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB uses no relative word before they had taken ("the catch … which they had taken").

5:10.sourceText: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάνην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου, οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι. καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν.
5:10.targetText: and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee.  “Do not be afraid,” Jesus said to Simon. “From now on you will catch men.”

groups.note: ὁμοίως … καί ("likewise also") is rendered so.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text (N1904: Ἰωάνην).
The relative clause οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοί ("who were partners") is rendered as the appositive his partners.
BSB renders τῷ Σίμωνι ("with Simon") as his.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB puts the quotation first and leaves this καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats the predicate of 5:9 (were astonished) for James and John; the Greek continues the objects of περιέσχεν.

5:11.sourceText: καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, ἀφέντες πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
5:11.targetText: And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him.

groups.note: The participle καταγαγόντες ("having brought") is rendered as a when-clause.
ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ("onto the land") is rendered ashore.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀφέντες, rendered left, to the main verb ἠκολούθησαν.

5:12.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας· ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν, πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς, δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
5:12.targetText: While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged Him, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive is a temporal while.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("he").
καὶ ἰδού ("and behold"), which brings in the main clause, is rendered by the presentational came along.
πλήρης ("full") is rendered covered.
The participle ἰδών ("having seen") is rendered as a When-clause.
ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ("on his face") is rendered facedown.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula Καὶ ἐγένετο ("and it came about") untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the comma before the quotation.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes the adjective πλήρης a relative clause; the Greek has no relative or copula.
English joins the participle πεσών, rendered fell, to the main verb ἐδεήθη.

5:13.sourceText: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ λέγων Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
5:13.targetText: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately the leprosy left him.

groups.note: BSB renders the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("him") as the man.
ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ ("went away from") is rendered left.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle ἐκτείνας.
English joins the participle ἐκτείνας, rendered reached out, to the main verb ἥψατο.

5:14.sourceText: καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς, εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
5:14.targetText: “Do not tell anyone,” Jesus instructed him. “But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτός ("he").
μηδενί ("no one") is rendered not … anyone.
The dative ἱερεῖ supplies to.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB puts the quotation first and leaves the verse-opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render καθώς ("just as"); Moses prescribed becomes a clause describing the offering.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for present; προσένεγκε has none in Luke.

5:15.sourceText: διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν·
5:15.targetText: But the news about Jesus spread all the more, and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for hear; ἀκούειν has none.

5:16.sourceText: αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος.
5:16.targetText: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.

groups.note: The periphrastic ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ("was withdrawing") is rendered as a habit, frequently withdrew.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders καὶ προσευχόμενος ("and praying") as a purpose infinitive without and.

5:17.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων, καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἱερουσαλήμ· καὶ δύναμις Κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι αὐτόν.
5:17.targetText: One day Jesus was teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea, and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.

groups.note: ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν ("on one of the days") is rendered One day.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτός ("he").
BSB starts a new sentence and renders the relative οἵ ("who") as People.
The periphrastic ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες is rendered had come.
The one ἐκ governs the whole list of places; English repeats from.
The articular infinitive τὸ ἰᾶσθαι is rendered to heal.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula Καὶ ἐγένετο ("and it came about") untranslated.
BSB leaves untranslated the καί that brings in the main clause after ἐγένετο.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a location; ἦσαν καθήμενοι has none.
English supplies an object for heal; αὐτόν is the subject of the infinitive.

5:18.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος, καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ θεῖναι ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.
5:18.targetText: Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus,

groups.note: καὶ ἰδού ("and behold") is rendered Just then.
φέροντες ("bringing") is rendered came carrying.
The relative clause ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος ("who was paralyzed") is rendered by the adjective paralyzed.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves this καί untranslated.
BSB joins the two infinitives without and, making the second a purpose.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here (a second him, after set), which N1904 lacks.

5:19.sourceText: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον, ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
5:19.targetText: but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.

groups.note: σύν ("with") is rendered on.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτόν ("they might bring him in"); a way stands for the whole clause.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a sequence word; the Greek participle ἀναβάντες has no connective.
English joins the participle ἀναβάντες, rendered went up, to the main verb καθῆκαν.
English specifies the middle of the crowd; the Greek says only "into the middle".

5:20.sourceText: καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἄνθρωπε, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου.
5:20.targetText: When Jesus saw their faith, He said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”

groups.note: The participle ἰδών ("having seen") is rendered as a When-clause.
The vocative Ἄνθρωπε ("man") is rendered Friend.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render σοι ("to you"); your already names the person.

5:21.sourceText: καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας; τίς δύναται ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ Θεός;
5:21.targetText: But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

groups.note: εἰ μή ("if not, except") is rendered but.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
λέγοντες ("saying") is represented only by the comma and quotation marks.

5:22.sourceText: ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
5:22.targetText: Knowing what they were thinking, Jesus replied, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?

groups.note: The noun διαλογισμούς ("thoughts") with its article is rendered as a clause, what they were thinking.
ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered by one verb.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render the addressee πρὸς αὐτούς ("to them").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for thinking; διαλογίζεσθε has none.

5:23.sourceText: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν Ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου, ἢ εἰπεῖν Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;
5:23.targetText: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render σοι ("to you"); Your already names the person.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:24.sourceText: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας, εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ Σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
5:24.targetText: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”

groups.note: The article and participle τῷ παραλελυμένῳ form one unit, "the paralyzed man".
This καί joins the main verbs ἔγειρε and πορεύου; English places the and before the last verb of the series.
εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου ("to your house") is rendered home.

5:25.sourceText: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν, ἄρας ἐφ’ ὃ κατέκειτο, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν Θεόν.
5:25.targetText: And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.

groups.note: εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ("to his house") is rendered home.

5:26.sourceText: καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας, καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν Θεόν, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι Εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον.

5:27.sourceText: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν, καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευεὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀκολούθει μοι.

5:28.sourceText: καὶ καταλιπὼν πάντα ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participles.

5:29.sourceText: Καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευεὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἦν ὄχλος πολὺς τελωνῶν καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετ’ αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι.
5:29.targetText: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text (N1904: Λευείς).

5:30.sourceText: καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε;

5:31.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες·
5:31.targetText: Jesus answered, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered by one verb.
χρείαν ἔχουσιν ("have need") is rendered need; who supplies its subject in the English cleft.

unmappedTarget.reason: English cleft frame; the Greek has no copula here.

5:32.sourceText: οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν.
5:32.targetText: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”

5:33.sourceText: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν Οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάνου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται, ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων, οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν.
5:33.targetText: Then they said to Him, “John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking.”

groups.note: In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text (N1904: Ἰωάνου).
δεήσεις ποιοῦνται ("they make prayers") is rendered pray.
ὁμοίως καί ("likewise also") is rendered and, joining the two groups.
οἱ σοί ("your ones") is rendered Yours.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:34.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος, ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν, ποιῆσαι νηστεῦσαι;
5:34.targetText: Jesus replied, “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?

groups.note: Μή marks a question expecting the answer no; BSB asks Can you.
υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος ("sons of the bridal chamber") is an idiom for wedding guests.
ἐν ᾧ ("in the time when") is rendered while.
ὁ νυμφίος ("the bridegroom") is rendered He.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
BSB does not render the addressee πρὸς αὐτούς ("to them").

5:35.sourceText: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι, καὶ ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
5:35.targetText: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.”

groups.note: ἡμέραι ("days") is rendered the time.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves this καί untranslated; the when-clause follows directly.
BSB leaves ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις ("in those days") untranslated; then gives the time.

5:36.sourceText: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, καὶ τὸ καινὸν σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ.
5:36.targetText: He also told them a parable: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.

groups.note: ἐπίβλημα ("patch") is rendered a piece of cloth.
The participle σχίσας ("having torn") is rendered as the finite tears.
ἐπιβάλλει ("puts on") is rendered sews.
ἱμάτιον ("garment") is rendered one.
εἰ δὲ μήγε ("otherwise", literally "but if not") is rendered If he does.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
ὅτι introduces the direct quotation and is represented by the colon and quotation marks.
This second article makes from the new a description of the patch; English needs no second the.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle σχίσας to the main verb ἐπιβάλλει.
English repeats the object of sews; the Greek states ἐπίβλημα once.

5:37.sourceText: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος ὁ νέος τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται·
5:37.targetText: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.

groups.note: εἰ δὲ μήγε ("otherwise", literally "but if not") is rendered If he does.
The pronoun αὐτός ("it") is rendered the wine.

unmappedSource.reason: This second article repeats the definite with νέος; English needs no second the.
BSB joins the clauses with commas and places its and before the last one.

5:38.sourceText: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς βλητέον.
5:38.targetText: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.

groups.note: The verbal adjective βλητέον ("must be put") is rendered is poured.

5:39.sourceText: καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν παλαιὸν θέλει νέον· λέγει γάρ Ὁ παλαιὸς χρηστός ἐστιν.
5:39.targetText: And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”

groups.note: The adjective παλαιόν stands for old wine.
χρηστός ("good") is rendered better, the comparison with new wine being implied.
